comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. One polygon, way/251260219 (Wildcat Mountain), which holds every lift and run of the resort. Two other winter_sports polygons reach into the box and are listed neighbours (resorts.json): Tuckerman Ravine, Mount Washington's backcountry bowl across Pinkham Notch, which is not Wildcat's (its gullies are left off), and Great Glen Trails, the nordic centre north on Route 16. Every named run and lift checked on 2026-11-12 against Wildcat's 2025-26 winter trail map (skiwildcat.com/the-mountain/about-the-mountain/trail-map.aspx, 20251226_WC_winter-trail_map_001.pdf, the James Niehues painting with its legend and mountain stats: 48 trails, 5 lifts), the only map the page lists (read with WebFetch), read from the PDF's full-size copy on the resort's image server (scene7, 3575 x 4990 px), tile by tile. The legend has Easier (green circle), More Difficult (blue square) and Most Difficult (one black diamond), as OSM's easy, intermediate and advanced, and Tree Skiing (a pattern of trees, each area marked with a black diamond); there is no double black and no terrain park. The resort's lift and terrain status page loads by script, so the printed map is the only source and wins. Of OSM's named runs, all carry the map's rating but Stray-Cat (blue on the map; easy in OSM). The painting writes its names with a dash between words (UPPER-CATAPULT, LOWER-POLECAT, TOP-CAT, MIDDLE-POLECAT, WILDCAT-EXPRESS-QUAD) and OSM follows it on some runs and not on others (Upper-Wildcat, Lower-Polecat, Lift-Lion, Black-Cat; Middle Polecat, Lower Lynx): names that differ from the map only by that separator, an apostrophe or a space stay as OSM has them, Leos-Leap (LEO'S LEAP) among them. Names from the map: Al's Folly (OSM Alls-Folly), Tomcat (OSM TopCat, the green trail from Cat-Track to Catnap; the map's TOP-CAT is the black trail from the summit, OSM's Top-Cat), The Chute (OSM The-Chutes), and capitals for Middle Wildcat, Lower Wildcat, Lower Cat Track and Snowcat Trail (OSM Middle wildcat, Lower wild cat, Lower cat track, Snowcat trail). OSM's CAt-Catofe, a 216 m blue way from Cat-Track's east end towards Upper-Wildcat, is on no source under that name (the map draws Cat-Track running on into Middle Wildcat there and labels no trail of its own), so it stays as OSM has it; reported. OSM's Easy Way (161 m, green, near the Tomcat Triple's base) is not labelled on the map either and stays. Lifts: the four chairs (Wildcat Express Quad, Tomcat Triple, Bobcat Triple, Snowcat Triple) are in OSM, none hidden. Hidden: the seven tree-skiing areas OSM draws only as closed outlines (natural=wood without area=yes, rated advanced; one named Tree Skiing, one with the loc_name Bonus Woods), which would draw as runs looping round the woods, as Okemo's and Copper Mountain's glade outlines are. Out of bounds: the Thompson Brook Trail (two ways of a path tagged downhill and backcountry, 2.4 km), on Wildcat Mountain's own north-east flank beyond the boundary the map draws along Polecat, is drawn out of bounds by the rule (37 % and 1 % of its ways inside the polygon). Mount Washington's backcountry across Pinkham Notch is left off whole: Tuckerman Ravine's gullies by the neighbour rule, and by hides the 16 lines outside that polygon in the Overpass window (the Gulf of Slides' five gullies and the Southern Snowfields' four ways on Boott Spur, six lines near the Lakes of the Clouds, two of them untagged, which would draw as unrated runs in bounds, and a touring line on the mountain's west side), all beyond the box's west edge. OSM gaps (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): Copy-Cat (blue, beside the Bobcat Triple), Ocelot Way (blue, at the Tomcat Triple's base), Cat & Mouse (green, by the lodge), the Snowbelt surface lift, and the tree-skiing areas as runs.

overrides.reason: Stray-Cat, from Middle Polecat along the northern boundary to the base, is drawn blue with the More Difficult square (STRAY-CAT) on Wildcat's 2025-26 winter trail map (skiwildcat.com/the-mountain/about-the-mountain/trail-map.aspx, 20251226_WC_winter-trail_map_001.pdf, the James Niehues painting, read from its full-size copy on the resort's image server); OSM rates it easy. The printed map wins.
